methodology.marketCapSource: Screener.in company pages, fetched 2026-08-11 (intraday). Figures in Rs crore as displayed. Volatile — treat as of that date only.
methodology.promoterHoldingSource: Screener.in shareholding-pattern tables (which reproduce SEBI/exchange quarterly shareholding filings). Quarter recorded per entity in asOfQuarter.
methodology.cinPolicy: A CIN is tiered 'documented' only where it was read off a primary document actually fetched (company letterhead on a media release, or the SEBI abridged prospectus). CINs whose only basis is an MCA-mirror aggregator page surfaced by search (ZaubaCorp, Tofler, FalconEbiz, IndiaFilings) are tiered 'reported' and flagged for re-verification against the MCA portal — see gaps.
methodology.registeredVsOperationalHq: hqCity/state/stateCode record the REGISTERED office. Where the operational centre differs (notably Jio Platforms and Reliance Jio Infocomm, registered in Ahmedabad, Gujarat but operationally headquartered at Reliance Corporate Park, Navi Mumbai), the operational reality is recorded in notes. Conflating the two is the most common error in state-wise corporate maps.
methodology.nullPolicy: Any figure, stake, CIN, ISIN or date not verified against a cited source is null, with the reason in notes or in gaps. No value in this file is estimated, inferred or interpolated.
methodology.outOfScope: The KG-D6 gas-pricing controversy, the CAG audit of the KG-D6 cost recovery, the RIL/RPL 2007 trades matter, and all other proceedings and allegations are OUT OF SCOPE. Where a proceeding is unavoidably visible in a primary document used here, it is recorded neutrally, attributed, and not treated as a finding.

disambiguation.twoAmbaniGroups: Two entirely separate 'Reliance' groups descend from Dhirubhai Ambani's business, divided between his sons in 2005. (1) MUKESH Ambani's Reliance Industries group — the subject of this file. (2) ANIL Ambani's Reliance Group (ADAG) — Reliance Power, Reliance Infrastructure, the former Reliance Communications. They share no common promoter entity. Anil Ambani's entities are recorded ONLY in the top-level separateAnilAmbaniGroup array, never in entities[], so that no downstream aggregation of group=='reliance' can merge them.
disambiguation.nameCollisions: 'Reliance' as a corporate name string is not a group identifier. Reliance Industrial Infrastructure Ltd (RIIL) IS in Mukesh Ambani's group (RIL holds 45.43%); Reliance Infrastructure Ltd (RELINFRA) is NOT. Two distinct MCA records are both named 'Reliance Retail Limited' — see gaps.

baseRateNotes: REFERENCE CLASS, FIXED BEFORE COUNTING: the ten large Indian conglomerate groups already catalogued in research/raw/conglomerates.json — reliance, adani, tata, aditya-birla, jsw, vedanta, bajaj, mahindra, lt, hinduja. Denominator = 10 for every rate below. This reference class was chosen because it is the pre-existing comparison set in this repository, not assembled after looking at Reliance.

IMPORTANT CAVEAT ON EVERY NUMERATOR BELOW: this file's research budget did not permit checking all ten groups against a source for each pattern. Every numerator stated is a VERIFIED FLOOR, not a final count. A floor with a stated denominator is usable; a numerator presented as complete when it is not would be worse than no number at all. The specific unchecked groups are named in each note and in gaps.

PM CARES CONTRIBUTION — verified floor 4/10 (40%) within 48 hours of the fund's creation. Documented from a single 30 March 2020 report: Tata Sons and Tata Trusts Rs 1,500 crore, Reliance Industries Rs 500 crore, Adani Group Rs 100 crore, JSW Group Rs 100 crore. Not checked: aditya-birla, vedanta, bajaj, mahindra, lt, hinduja. Direction of the error is one-way — the true rate can only be higher, since these are contributions announced in the first two days. The evidence-tiering table puts >=80% at 'non-discriminating' and 40-80% at 'weak, only usable with a control group and an effect size'. On the verified floor alone, a Reliance PM CARES contribution is at best a WEAK signal and is more likely non-discriminating. It should not be rendered as a finding. Falsifier for treating it as distinctive: a complete list of the ten groups' 2020-21 PM CARES contributions showing most did not contribute.

DoT SPECTRUM WON AT AUCTION — verified floor 2/10 (20%). Reliance (Reliance Jio Infocomm, 2010 BWA, 2021, 2022 and 2024 auctions) and Adani (Adani Data Networks participated in and took spectrum in the 2022 5G auction). Aditya Birla is a co-promoter of Vodafone Idea, an active bidder in the 2021, 2022 and 2024 auctions, which would make 3/10 — but the Aditya Birla to Vodafone Idea promoter link was NOT verified from any source fetched for this file (Screener's IDEA page does not name the promoters), so it is excluded from the numerator and recorded as a gap. No comparable check was run on the other nine groups, and SWF stakes in unlisted arms are typically disclosed only in offer documents, which most of these groups have not filed. Publishing '1/1' or an impressionistic 'Reliance has unusually many' would be exactly the base-rate neglect the pattern-discipline skill warns against. The honest statement is: Reliance's SWF exposure is well documented BECAUSE Jio Platforms filed a DRHP; comparable disclosure does not exist for most of the reference class, so the observed difference may be a DISCLOSURE ARTEFACT rather than a real difference in SWF penetration.
